title: Deconstructing the Global Cancer Manifold
text:
Cancer as Structural Perturbation
This project presents a global structural analysis of cancer transcriptomes using complexity theory, entropy analysis, spectral geometry, and nonlinear latent-space modeling.
The framework treats malignancy not simply as altered gene expression, but as a perturbation of transcriptomic organization itself.
The website is organized around two complementary levels of analysis:
Individual cancer comparisons are then interpreted within these larger structural state spaces.
Cancer is traditionally studied through genes, pathways, mutations, and differential expression. While these approaches have produced enormous biological insight, they do not fully address a broader systems-level question:
The Global Cancer Structural Inference Framework approaches cancer as a perturbation of transcriptomic organization.
Rather than focusing exclusively on individual genes or pathways, the framework investigates how malignancy alters:
The central hypothesis is that tumorigenesis may produce reproducible perturbational organization across multiple complementary representations of transcriptomic organization.

title: Deconstructing the Global Cancer Manifold
text:
First-Order Geometry
First-order geometry describes:

where tumor systems occupy structural state space.

The canonical structural map currently uses:

x-axis = complexity effective-rank delta
y-axis = entropy spectral delta

Alternative structural projections examine the same systems through additional coordinate formulations. The goal is to determine whether tumors occupy reproducible regions of transcriptomic organizational space rather than exhibiting entirely random structural disruption.

title: Deconstructing the Global Cancer Manifold
text:
Second-Order Geometry
Second-order geometry evaluates:

whether first-order structural locations remain stable across representational perturbations.

These analyses include:

cross-engine concordance,
platform reproducibility,
filter-regime trajectories,
quadrant stability,
robustness profiling,
boundary sensitivity,
and structural archetype persistence.

title: 2  First-Order Perturbational Geometry
text:
3 Purpose
This chapter introduces the first-order structural geometry of the Global Cancer Structural Inference Framework.
First-order geometry asks:
Each point in the following plots represents a normal–tumor comparison under a specific chip and filter-regime condition. The axes are not genes, pathways, or PCA components. They are structural descriptors derived from the complexity, entropy, MP spectral, and latent-geometry engines.
The goal is to visualize malignancy as an organizational perturbation of transcriptomic structure.

title: 3  Second-Order Stability Geometry
text:
4 Purpose
This chapter introduces second-order structural geometry.
Second-order geometry asks:

Are the first-order structural locations stable, recurrent, boundary-sensitive, or representation-dependent?

Where first-order geometry maps the location of tumor systems in structural state space, second-order geometry evaluates the stability and reproducibility of those locations across chips, filter regimes, engines, and quadrant boundaries.


5 Conceptual Scope
Second-order geometry includes:

quadrant stability,
boundary distance,
robustness class,
filter-regime trajectory length,
chip reproducibility,
engine agreement,
engine discordance,
and structural archetype persistence.

9.0.1 LU/LUAD: Biological Gene-Set Structural Report






Note



This report is exploratory and downstream of the structural-inference framework. It summarizes GO, KEGG, and MSigDB/Hallmark gene-set results associated with a single normal–tumor comparison. Biological terms are interpreted as annotations of structurally characterized tumor states, not as the primary evidentiary basis of the framework.
